claims.claim: LinkedIn's 2026 algorithm is keyword-driven (semantic search) not hashtag-driven; it removed hashtag following entirely (phased out through late 2024); 0-3 hashtags is the norm and hashtags no longer boost reach; it leans on the Interest Graph over the Relationship Graph (surfacing posts to topically-interested non-followers); 'saves' are a top engagement signal ahead of likes; dwell time is a major ranking signal; document/PDF carousels and native video far outperform plain text for reach. The first ~60 minutes ('golden hour') are an algorithmic test window: engagement and author replies in the first 15-60 minutes determine whether the post is amplified, so being present to reply fast (and not stacking a second post same-day) is a key reach lever.
claims.raw_snippet: Document posts hit 6.6% engagement, video grew 36% YoY, and newsletters deliver directly to inboxes, bypassing the algorithm entirely. This guide covers what the algorithm rewards now, with format benchmarks and a testing framework. ‍ The LinkedIn algorithm changed dramatically entering 2026, driven by LinkedIn's new unified AI ranking system 360Brew that replaced the legacy content infrastructure.

claims.claim: LinkedIn RECOMMENDS, rather than requires, that you let others know, if it is not obvious from the context, when you have relied heavily on AI to help create or modify content. There is no LinkedIn policy named 'Keeping conversations real'.
claims.raw_snippet: we recommend that you let others know
claims.note: The previous cycle attributed a named policy, 'Keeping conversations real', to LinkedIn and described disclosure as expected. That string occurs zero times on this page and zero times in the Professional Community Policies, so the name was not LinkedIn's and the obligation was overstated. The replacement snippet WAS read directly on the live page by two independent methods on 2026-08-27: a browser fetch with location.href asserted, and a plain curl whose raw HTML contains the string exactly once. The bundled --check-sources fetcher reports it missing, which is a fetcher difference on linkedin.com and not an absent quote. Full sentence: "we recommend that you let others know (if it isn't obvious from the context) if you've relied heavily on AI to help create or modify the content".
